sources: CRA T4127 Payroll Deductions Formulas (Jan 2026), recorded in salary/ and b4/ · 2026 · federal 14% to $58,523 then 20.5%; federal BPA $16,452; Manitoba 10.8% to $47,000 then 12.75%; Manitoba BPA $15,780

CRA / ESDC 2026 CPP figures (Investment Executive, Advisor.ca reports of the CRA announcement; b4/) · 2026 · 5.95% each for employee and employer, 11.9% self-employed, basic exemption $3,500, YMPE $74,600

CRA Schedule 8 (CPP on self-employment and other earnings) and lines 22200 / 31000 (via search summaries) · 2026 · employment and self-employment earnings are combined on one schedule, so the $3,500 exemption is applied once; self-employed CPP covers both halves; half is deductible (line 22200) with the enhanced part, the base part is a credit (line 31000)

Calculation (not a CRA rule): b9/calc.py. Case 1: $10,000 net self-employment income only → taxable income $9,548.25, below both basic personal amounts → $0 income tax; CPP (10,000 − 3,500) × 11.9% = $773.50. Case 2: on top of a $60,000 salary → extra federal $1,838.23 + Manitoba $1,132.93 = $2,971.15 income tax, CPP 10,000 × 11.9% = $1,190, total $4,161.15 (41.6%). Assumptions: Manitoba, single, 2026, $10,000 is net (after expenses), no other income or credits beyond the basics. Dependencies: province, other income, deductions/credits. Verification note: canada.ca cannot be opened from the build machine; the Schedule 8 exemption-sharing mechanic is from the form's structure (search summary). Check Schedule 8 on canada.ca before publishing.

titles: $10K Side Hustle in Canada: How Much Tax Do You Pay?
Same $10K Side Income, Two Very Different Tax Bills (Canada)
$774 or $4,161? The Tax on a $10K Side Hustle
yt.description:
$10,000 from your channel or side hustle. How much tax do you pay in Canada? It depends on one thing: what else you earn.

Case 1 — it's your only income (Manitoba, 2026): taxable income is under the basic personal amount, so $0 income tax. But self-employed CPP still applies: ($10,000 − $3,500) × 11.9% = $773.50.

Case 2 — the same $10,000 on top of a $60,000 salary: every extra dollar lands in your top bracket, about $2,971 in income tax, plus $1,190 of CPP (both halves; your job already used the $3,500 exemption). Total: $4,161 — more than five times the bill.

On a $100,000 salary? Say yes in the comments and we'll run it next.

Sources: CRA T4127 (2026 rates), CRA CPP 2026, Schedule 8. Example only (Manitoba, single, $10K net, basic credits); general information, not tax advice.
